title: State existence unproved in general; non-modular reducts admit no separating state

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Severity: major (load-bearing scope/existence claim).**

The numerical theory is summarized throughout (Abstract, Remark "precise dichotomy", Theorem "main", §8) as holding *"for every complete residuated lattice carrying a state"*, and the framework is advertised as a satisfactory generalization "in numerical $[0,1]$-valued form for every lattice carrying a state." But the ONLY existence result, Proposition "States exist for the standard algebras", covers exclusively **finite Heyting algebras, finite MV-algebras, and finite products**. There is no theorem characterizing which complete residuated lattices admit a state.

Two concrete problems:

1. **Infinite non-chain $L$**: no state and no measure are produced (e.g. an infinite Heyting algebra, or $[0,1]^2$ with componentwise product t-norm). The headline "every complete residuated lattice" is unsupported here.

2. **Non-modular lattice reducts make a separating state IMPOSSIBLE.** Axiom (S3) $s(x\vee y)+s(x\wedge y)=s(x)+s(y)$ is a *modular valuation*. By Birkhoff's lattice theory, a strictly isotone modular valuation exists iff the lattice is modular. The critic verified symbolically on the pentagon $N_5$ (elements $0<a<b<1$, and $c$ incomparable to $a,b$): the constraints
$$s(a\vee c)+s(a\wedge c)=s(a)+s(c)\Rightarrow 1=s(a)+s(c),$$
$$s(b\vee c)+s(b\wedge c)=s(b)+s(c)\Rightarrow 1=s(b)+s(c),$$
**force $s(a)=s(b)$** even though $a\ne b$. Hence on a residuated lattice whose reduct is non-modular, NO state separates points; the numerical $\rho_s$ collapses distinct $\not\approx$-classes and the claim "metric/separating for every lattice" is false.

**Required fix.** Replace the "every complete residuated lattice" prose with a precise dichotomy: state existence (and top-faithfulness) requires modularity of the reduct (for finite $L$, iff the reduct is modular); for non-modular reducts prove the obstruction that no separating state exists. This is exactly the kind of "obstruction" part (c) of the problem asks for, and is currently missing.
